LAW 200.title: Indigenous Settler Legal Relations
LAW 200.description: Critical examination of the history and legacy of colonial legal orders in Canada. This course is compulsory for students who commence their Juris Doctor degree in September 2020 or later.

LAW 201.title: Indigenous Peoples and Law
LAW 201.description: Critical examination of the history and legacy of colonial legal orders in Canada and their impacts on First Nations, Métis, Inuit and urban Indigenous Peoples, and overview of sources and authorities of Indigenous laws, Indigenous legal theories and methodologies, and the unique constitutional status and rights of Aboriginal Peoples in Canada.

LAW 202.title: Advocacy

LAW 211.title: Contracts

LAW 221.title: Criminal Law and Procedure
LAW 221.description: Bases of criminal responsibility; principles and objectives of the criminal law and procedure; pre-trial procedure.

LAW 231.title: Property Law

LAW 241.title: Torts
LAW 241.description: A study of the bases of civil liability for intentionally and accidentally caused harms.

LAW 251.title: Public Law
LAW 251.description: An overview of the constitutional and statutory law governing the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of government in Canada, including an introduction to statutory construction and analysis and the administration of law in Canada.

LAW 271.title: Introduction to Public Law and the Charter
LAW 271.description: An introduction to the structure, powers, duties of and relationships among the various institutions and actors that comprise the Canadian state, the principles of statutory interpretation, and the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

LAW 281.title: Legal Research and Writing

LAW 291.title: Aboriginal and Treaty Rights

LAW 300.title: Jurisprudence and Critical Perspectives

LAW 301.title: Philosophy of Law
LAW 301.description: An examination of the principal schools of legal theory, such as legal positivism, legal realism, sociological jurisprudence, and contemporary rights theory. Not offered each year, consult Faculty.

LAW 302.title: Fundamental Concepts of Law
